system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
| Issue | Seller’s position | Buyer should want | Recommendation (with one-line reason) |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001: General liability cap** | General Warranty Claims capped at **20% of price (AUD 4.8m)**. | A materially higher cap, sized to the diligence and risk profile; separate higher caps for specific risks where appropriate. | **Reject as drafted; negotiate a higher general cap.** A 20% cap may leave the Buyer bearing substantial losses from warranty breaches. |
| **SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket** | AUD 25,000 de minimis and AUD 250,000 tipping basket, with only the excess recoverable. | A lower de minimis and a tipping basket (recovery from dollar one once crossed), or a lower deductible basket if the Seller insists. | **Seek a lower threshold and tipping basket.** The proposed deductible basket leaves the Buyer absorbing the first AUD 250,000 even after claims cross the threshold. |
| **SPA-N-003: General claims time limit** | Claims notified within 18 months; Seller also proposes applying any limitation to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise. | A longer general warranty period (commonly negotiated by reference to the business and diligence); distinct periods for tax, fundamental and specific claims, with proper survival and notice mechanics. | **Reject the blanket approach; negotiate differentiated periods.** Eighteen months may be too short, and a general limit should not silently truncate other claim categories. |
| **SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title warranties subject to general caps and time limits. | Separate, substantially higher cap (potentially up to the price or full consideration) and longer period for fundamental/title claims. | **Reject; ring-fence fundamental/title claims.** A general-warranty cap and short period are inadequate for ownership or authority defects. |
| **SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims; no express fraud carve-out is stated. | Express carve-outs for fraud and deliberate or intentional misconduct (including relevant seller-side conduct), from caps, thresholds, time bars, exclusive remedy and non-reliance, to the extent legally permissible. | **Require an express carve-out.** The documents should not allow contractual limitations to shield fraud. |
| **SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope** | Broad general disclosure of the data room, Accounts, registers and public records; specific disclosures also provided. | Specific, fair disclosure against each relevant warranty, with sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope of the matter; no blanket data-room or public-record deemed disclosure. | **Reject general disclosure as a warranty qualifier.** It can defeat meaningful warranty protection without identifying what was disclosed against which warranty. |
| **SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier** | No claim for matters known by Buyer or advisers, including anything discoverable from data room or public records. | At most, a narrow actual-knowledge qualifier for named individuals, excluding constructive/imputed knowledge and preserving claims for matters merely discoverable. | **Reject as drafted.** A discoverability standard converts diligence access into a broad waiver and creates uncertainty over whose knowledge counts. |
| **SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent** | Seller will use reasonable endeavours; consent treated as satisfied on delivery of counterparty’s written consent. DD-002 shows ~AUD 3.6m FY26 revenue (~30%), but no final consent or evidence conditions are satisfied. | A condition to Completion requiring final written consent and satisfaction/waiver of all associated conditions, with termination or other protection if not obtained. | **Make this a genuine completion condition, not merely delivery of consent.** The customer is material and the disclosed consent conditions remain unverified. |
| **SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility** | ~AUD 3.2m facility to be released after Completion. DD-003 says it remains outstanding and no final discharge is included. | Repayment at or before Completion from the agreed funds flow, with lender payout evidence and release/discharge of all security as a completion deliverable. | **Do not defer release until after Completion.** The Buyer should not acquire the company with debt or security still outstanding. |
| **SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses** | AUD 420,000 conditional Completion bonuses are not separately itemised in the draft funds flow; payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs are unspecified. | Identify and settle or deduct the full cost—including applicable on-costs—in the funds flow/price mechanics, with supporting calculations and no double recovery. | **Require reconciliation before signing/completion.** An unprovided-for completion liability can undermine the agreed price and debt-free/cash-free basis. |
| **SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity** | Existing indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; DD-004/010 show transfer depends on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee, AUD 180,000 is open, and no payment receipt or confirmatory assignment is in the data room. | Payment and effective assignment of all required IP before Completion, backed by a specific indemnity covering title, access, use and related loss if transfer fails or is challenged. | **Expand and secure the protection; require evidence of cleared payment and assignment.** The disclosed condition may leave critical project materials untransferred. |
| **SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident** | Treated as preliminary and not expected to be material; DD-006 describes a link sent to an unintended external email, potentially ~1,240 records, with access, scope and notification status unresolved. | Complete investigation and remediation, required notices, full disclosure, and a specific indemnity or tailored protection for incident-related liabilities and costs. | **Do not rely on the Seller’s materiality view; seek targeted protection.** The facts are unresolved and may generate regulatory, response and third-party costs. |
| **SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals** | Three renewals totalling AUD 330,000 described as ordinary-course operating costs; DD-008/011 do not establish whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course. | Confirm contractual status, timing, termination rights and accrual; include any pre-Completion accrued/unavoidable amounts in the agreed price/debt-like treatment or specific protection. | **Seek evidence and reconcile in the completion accounts/funds flow.** The aggregate commitment is material enough that its treatment cannot be assumed from the Seller’s label. |
| **SPA-N-014: Category separation** | Seller says limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to all Claims; tax and IP are said to be settled under the general regime. | Expressly separate warranty, tax, title/fundamental, specific indemnity, debt/funds-flow and other claims, with tailored caps, thresholds, time limits and remedies. | **Reject “all Claims” treatment; draft category-specific rules.** A single regime risks inadvertently cutting down negotiated indemnities and non-warranty remedies. |
| **SPA-N-015: Title verification** | Seller relies on DD-012 share register showing it as holder of 100%; no independent Buyer verification is stated. | Verify register and corporate records, issued capital, encumbrances and transfer authority; obtain title warranty and clean transfer deliverables. | **Treat DD-012 as evidence to verify, not conclusive proof.** A register entry alone does not resolve all title, capacity or encumbrance risks. |
| **SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms** | Seller considers tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime. | Negotiate explicit tax and IP warranty scope, separate caps/time limits where warranted, and ensure specific indemnities (including Ironquay) are not diluted by general limitations. | **Keep these terms open until expressly agreed.** The Seller’s assertion does not resolve the missing protections or the disclosed IP transfer issue. |

These are buyer-side negotiation recommendations based on the supplied extracts, not a substitute for reviewing the full SPA, schedules, disclosure materials and funds flow with Australian transaction counsel.
=== END ADVICE ===
